title: Bounty Opera
notes: This recipe is one of the more difficult in this book, but it's actually one of the more straightforward recipes on the Mosquito menu! Don't think of it as one big recipe, but rather a series of small ones. This recipe needs to be made the day before serving so it's great for a dinner party.

methodSections.heading: Joconde Sponge
steps: Whisk the whole eggs in a bench mixer with the icing sugar until the mixture has tripled in volume and formed a thick sabayon. Transfer this mixture to a large bowl and wash the mixer bowl and the whisk.
Place the egg whites into the clean bench mixer bowl and start whisking until they become foamy. Slowly sprinkle in the sugar and continue whisking until a thick glossy meringue forms.
Sift the almond flour and cake flour into the sabayon and fold through gently with a spatula.
Gently fold the meringue into the sabayon/flour mixture until it is just combined.

Working quickly, spread the batter on a half sheet baking tray (18"x13") lined with parchment paper with an offset spatula as evenly as possible. Bake at 195°C (380°F) for 5-6 minutes or until the sponge colour changes slightly. Let cool completely before constructing the opera.

methodSections.heading: Coconut Spread
steps: Soak the gelatine in ice water to bloom.

In a heavy-based saucepan over a medium heat, stir together the coconut purée, brown sugar and cornstarch until the cornstarch activates and thickens the mixture. When thick, remove from the heat and stir in the bloomed gelatine and then the toasted coconut.
Reserve this mixture in a warm place for the construction of opera.

methodSections.heading: Malibu Syrup
steps: Boil together the water and sugar to dissolve the sugar. Let this syrup cool completely.
Add in the Malibu and lime zest and reserve this mixture for the construction of the Opera Cake.

methodSections.heading: Opera Cake Construction
steps: Melt the chocolate over a bain-marie of slowly simmering water.

Cut the Joconde Sponge into 3 even portions, each portion being 6"x13". Paint the top side of one joconde layer with the melted chocolate and then place in the fridge to set. This will become the very bottom of the cake and stops the Malibu Syrup from soaking out of the finished bars.
When set, flip the chocolate-painted joconde upside down and place back into its baking tray chocolate side down. Peel the parchment paper off what is now the top of the joconde.
Brush the joconde generously with the Malibu Syrup.
Divide the coconut spread evenly into two portions and spread the first portion over the Malibu-soaked joconde.
Flip the second layer of joconde onto the layer of coconut spread and peel the parchment paper off the back. Brush this layer generously with the Malibu Syrup.
Put the remainder of the coconut spread on top of this and spread it evenly over the joconde.
Flip the third layer of joconde onto the cake and remove the parchment paper. Once again apply a liberal amount of the Malibu Syrup.
The Opera Cake is now constructed and needs to be placed in the freezer overnight to freeze completely.

methodSections.heading: Coconut Chantilly
steps: Soak the gelatine in ice water to bloom.
In a heavy-based saucepan, mix together the coconut purée, glucose, trimoline and salt, and bring to a boil. Add in the bloomed gelatine and whisk to combine.
Place the white chocolate into a bowl. Strain the hot coconut mixture through a fine mesh sieve over the chocolate and let sit for 30 seconds to melt the chocolate. Whisk to combine.
Add the cream into the coconut white chocolate mixture and whisk to combine.
Refrigerate overnight to let rest so it doesn't split when whipped.

methodSections.heading: Coconut Glaze
steps: Remove the fully frozen Opera Cake from the freezer and portion into the desired serving size. Place back into the freezer to keep frozen.
Place the two types of chocolate together in a bain-marie and melt over slowly simmering water.
Once the chocolates have melted, slowly emulsify the oil into the chocolate until completely incorporated. Stir in the toasted coconut.
Let the mixture cool to 28-30°C (82-86°F) and then use a fork to dip each of the frozen Opera Cake portions ensuring all the sides and top are coated.

methodSections.heading: Passionfruit Tapioca Sauce
steps: Bring the water and sugar to a rolling boil and then add the tapioca pearls. Reduce the heat until the pearls are gently boiling. The water should be moving fast enough that the individual pearls of tapioca are rolling about and not sticking together in clumps.

In a separate saucepan, place passionfruit purée, mango purée, sugar, kaffir lime leaves, ginger and vanilla bean. Bring to a boil to dissolve the sugar and then remove from the heat and let the flavours infuse.

The tapioca has finished cooking when the pearls become translucent and the water has reduced enough to form a thicker consistency liquid. Remove from the heat and strain the passionfruit liquid through a fine mesh sieve into the cooked tapioca.
Let the tapioca sauce cool to room temperature before refrigerating.

methodSections.heading: Chocolate Ice Cream
steps: Mix the pectin with the sugar and set aside.
Melt chocolate over a bain-marie of slowly simmering water.
In a heavy-based saucepan, combine the cream, glucose and trimoline. Bring mixture to a boil and then whisk in the pectin-sugar mixture. Boil for a minute longer then remove from the heat.
Add the milk to the cream mixture and then emulsify into the melted chocolate.
Cool over ice and then churn into ice cream as following your ice cream machine's instructions.

methodSections.heading: To Plate and Garnish
steps: Whip the Coconut Chantilly to soft peaks and then pipe onto the top of the Bounty Opera bar.
Drizzle the passionfruit tapioca sauce creatively around the serving plate.
Place the bar slightly off centre on the plate.
Place a prepared rectangular piece of tempered chocolate into the piped Coconut Chantilly on top of the bar.
Sprinkle some toasted coconut flakes along one side of the tempered chocolate and a small spoonful next to the bounty bar to hold the ice cream in place on the plate.
Place a viola on the bar as a garnish and finish with a quenelle of chocolate ice cream.
